symbols.note: String constant 'memory/events.local.jsonl' used as stable journal identity.

claims.text: The journal (``memory/events.local.jsonl``) is authoritative.
claims.why: No code in this chunk establishes authoritativeness; it depends on the write path and other modules.

claims.text: Nothing in the operational append path is allowed to block on an embedding call, so this worker is the *only* component that is supposed to move the index forward
claims.why: This claim references the append path and embedding call policy, which are not shown in this chunk.

claims.text: it is also the component that owns :meth:`EventVectorStore.record_journal_watermark`
claims.why: EventVectorStore and its method are imported from .embeddings but not defined here; ownership claim cannot be verified.

claims.text: Before it existed, every search reported ``freshness == 'unanchored'``: freshness unknown.
claims.why: Refers to historical behaviour not present in this chunk.

claims.text: Progress is a byte offset into the journal, stored as a :class:`JournalPosition` watermark inside the index itself.
claims.why: JournalPosition is imported but not defined here; the watermark storage mechanism is not shown.

claims.text: A run starts at the recorded watermark, never at zero, so restarting is cheap.
claims.why: No code in this chunk shows the start-up logic.

claims.text: the index is content-addressed (``UNIQUE(index_id, source_hash)`` with ``INSERT OR IGNORE``), so a replayed entry *cannot* duplicate
claims.why: Refers to database schema not present in this chunk.

claims.text: this worker filters entries whose ``source_hash`` is already in the index *before* embedding them, so a replay also costs nothing.
claims.why: No code in this chunk implements such filtering.

claims.text: If the filter were wrong in the direction of 'not yet projected', the result is redundant embedding work, never a duplicate row and never a lost entry.
claims.why: Hypothetical analysis not backed by code in this chunk.

claims.text: A watermark is recorded only after the projections for every journal byte below it are committed.
claims.why: No code in this chunk shows watermark recording logic.

claims.text: The crash window is therefore one batch wide and it always fails *behind*
claims.why: Crash recovery behaviour not shown.

claims.text: the reverse -- a watermark ahead of the vectors -- is never written, because that would silently drop journal entries forever.
claims.why: No code in this chunk prevents such a scenario.

claims.text: ``content_hash`` on the watermark is the SHA-256 of the journal prefix ``[0, position)``.
claims.why: No code in this chunk computes content_hash.

claims.text: On every run that prefix is re-hashed. A journal that was rewritten, truncated, or replaced fails the check and the run refuses with ``journal_forked``
claims.why: No check logic in this chunk.

claims.text: Only complete lines are consumed. A trailing line with no ``\n`` is a writer mid-append, not a record. The watermark stops before it.
claims.why: No line-reading logic in this chunk.

claims.text: Consuming it would parse a fragment and then skip the real record forever.
claims.why: Hypothetical scenario not backed by code in this chunk.

claims.text: ``embedder_unavailable`` is an outage: the run stops, keeps the watermark it earned, and exits non-zero
claims.why: No error handling code in this chunk.

claims.text: ``model_drift`` is a correctness fault that survives a retry: :mod:`daedalus.memory.embeddings` refuses *before* writing, and this worker neither catches that refusal nor advances past it.
claims.why: Refers to code in embeddings.py not present here.

claims.text: The worker resolves its :class:`EmbeddingSpec` **without calling the backend**: either by adopting the one index already recorded for this (provider, model, revision, normalization, projector) identity, or from the declared ``dimension`` (default :data:`DEFAULT_DIMENSION`).
claims.why: No resolution logic in this chunk.

claims.text: That is what makes 'a second run over an unchanged journal does zero embedding work' true rather than approximately true -- a probe call to discover the dimension would break it.
claims.why: No code in this chunk demonstrates zero-embedding behaviour.

claims.text: ``model_revision`` defaults to ``None`` on purpose.
claims.why: No code in this chunk sets a default for model_revision.

claims.text: The shipped reader, ``daedalus.context_plan.latent_memory_seed_scores``, searches with no spec, so the spec it resolves has ``model_revision=None``.
claims.why: Refers to external module not provided.

claims.text: Pinning a revision here produces a *different* ``index_id``, and ``daedalus context --latent`` would report ``index_unavailable`` against a perfectly good index.
claims.why: No code in this chunk ties revision to index_id or reports index_unavailable.

claims.text: The worker warns when a revision is pinned.
claims.why: No warning logic in this chunk.

claims.text: Drift is still caught, empirically, by the identity anchor in :mod:`daedalus.memory.embeddings`
claims.why: Refers to embeddings.py not provided.

claims.text: One run reads every unprojected complete line before batching. ``--limit`` is the bound for a journal that has grown far beyond what one run should chew through; there is no streaming path.
claims.why: No batch reading logic in this chunk.

claims.text: Position is a byte offset, and only compares to byte offsets. A caller that measures the same journal in line counts and passes that as a :class:`JournalPosition` will get a meaningless freshness answer.
claims.why: No comparison logic in this chunk.

claims.text: Use :func:`journal_position` on both sides.
claims.why: journal_position function not defined in this chunk; likely in embeddings.py.

claims.text: A malformed or blank line is stepped over, not retried. Both are counted and named in the report, and the watermark advances past them
claims.why: No line processing logic in this chunk.

claims.text: Nothing here schedules anything. The index goes stale the moment the next event is appended. Freshness is now *answerable*; keeping it fresh is a scheduling decision this module does not make.
claims.why: No scheduling code in this chunk.

claims.text: Run it: python -m daedalus.memory.projection_worker --json
claims.why: No __main__ block in this chunk.
